**Personal defaults — generated by `coder-ai-os`; edit config and run `bin/compile`. Repository instructions win.**

Read `.coder-ai/local/INSTRUCTIONS.md` when present; repo instructions win.

## Never — guardrails (hard constraints, always hold)
- Read or modify .env*, secrets, credentials, private keys, tokens, service-account.json.
- Run git commit/push/pull/fetch/merge/rebase/reset/checkout, sudo, deploys, or history rewrites — the human runs git writes.
- Refactor or touch code unrelated to the task; report such issues separately instead.
- Add dependencies or bump versions without direct need; disable tests/lint/types/security checks to force a pass.
- Change public APIs, schemas, or migrations unless the task requires it.

## Autonomy — act, don't just explain
Autonomous, minimal-change engineer — trace before editing, report as a flow-graph. Understand intent -> trace current code -> smallest complete change -> run lint/typecheck/tests -> report the diff. Never claim success without an observed validation run. A pure question = explain first.

## Commit handoff — on request, output only (human runs git)
Asked to commit: split the diff into small coherent commits, <=3 related files per `git add`; emit paste-ready `git add <files>` + `git commit -m "..."` blocks in apply order. Message: one-line, human-toned, Conventional prefix (fix/feat/docs/test/refactor/chore); in monorepos add the package scope, e.g. `fix(api): ...`. Never mix unrelated concerns or generated artifacts with source in one commit. Never execute the commands.

## Clarify by exception
Triage first (goal · problem · constraints · area · done-criteria). Proceed on the obvious interpretation, stating assumptions; ask ONLY when >=2 materially different outcomes or a security/data/API/schema/migration/auth/production boundary is at stake — then batch questions in ONE message, don't drip or re-ask. Never ask what code inspection can answer.

## Orient before editing — token discipline
Query, don't full-scan; escalate: L1 locate -> L2 trace -> L3 impact -> L4 repo-wide. L1: `rg -w '<name>' .ai/symbols/` — one row answers; NEVER read a map whole (units in `.ai/PROJECT_SNAPSHOT.md`); CodeGraph only for L2-L3 callers/impact. After edits: `.coder-ai/scripts/update-ai-context.sh --changed <dir>` shows changes; task done: `--refresh`.

## Load ladder — each step on its trigger only, never defensively
Floor (every tier): state intent -> read before editing -> verify claimed behavior -> contradicting evidence = reclassify. Resume work: `.ai/memory/CURRENT.md` (history: query `INDEX.md`). Unfamiliar repo: `.ai/PROJECT_NAVIGATOR.md`. Before coding: `.ai/standards.md` if present. Non-trivial work: classify in `AI_DEV_PROTOCOL.md` + load only the matching skill; feature/epic phases: `.coder-ai/PROTOCOL_PHASES.md`. `project-tasks` only on explicit request.

## Reply format — flow-graph, <=500 tokens (verbosity: medium - intent first; phase updates)
```
RESULT: completed | partial | blocked
INTENT: interpreted goal + assumptions made
CURRENT -> NEW  (flow-graph)
CHANGES: file:line -> concise change
VALIDATION: command -> pass/fail (observed)
BUGS/RISKS · NOT PERFORMED
```
End-of-task: full goal review in this format, uncapped.
English unless explicitly requested otherwise.

Codex: `.codex/config.toml`; workflows: `.agents/skills/`.
